newsitem.title: VATICAN: Annan, Pope discuss Zaire, Mideast, Balkans.
newsitem.headline: Annan, Pope discuss Zaire, Mideast, Balkans.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan discussed Zaire, the Balkans and the Middle East with Pope John Paul on Tuesday.
Annan, meeting the Pope for the first time since he was elected U.N. leader, held about 25 minutes of talks with the Polish Pontiff in his private study at the Vatican.
A Vatican statement issued after the audience said the two discussed "the drama of the Great Lakes region as well as the Holy Land and the situation in the Balkans."
The 76-year-old Pope last weekend made an historic visit to the Bosnian capital Sarajevo and appealed to the Balkan country's wartime foes to seek reconciliation.
During a picture-taking session at the end of the private talks, the Pope told Annan: "God bless your families and your mission and God bless the United Nations."
Annan, who is on a visit to Italy, called the Pope "a father to all."
On Monday Annan appealed to U.N. members to press Zaire's rebel leader Laurent Kabila to seek a negotiated solution through a ceasefire and sustained talks on the country's future.
The Pope has also made numerous appeals for an end to the violence in Zaire.
The Pontiff, who has suffered a series of health problems in recent years, appeared in good form during the public part of the audience.
